text: Asha is picked only if Bilal is picked.
why: If Asha is picked, Bilal must be. Bilal can still be picked without Asha.

text: The team bats first only if it wins the toss.
why: Batting first needs a won toss. Winning the toss and choosing to bowl is still allowed.

text: Chitra goes to the fair if Dev goes.
why: "P if Q" puts the condition after "if": if Dev goes, Chitra goes. Chitra may also go alone.

text: Ravi is not promoted without passing the test.
why: "Not P without Q" is "P only if Q". Passing is needed, but it does not guarantee a promotion.

text: Passing the interview is necessary for Esha to get the job.
np: She does not get the job
why: A necessary condition is the "only if" part: the job needs the interview passed, not the other way round.

text: Winning the semi-final is enough to get a medal.
why: A sufficient condition is the "if" part: win the semi-final, and a medal follows. A medal can still come another way.

text: The shop opens on Sunday only when the owner is in town.
why: "Only when" works like "only if": an open shop on Sunday means the owner is in town.

text: Farhan sits at an end only if Gita sits next to him.
np: Farhan is not at an end
nq: Gita is not next to him
why: Farhan at an end forces Gita beside him. Gita can sit beside him when he is in the middle too.

text: The match is replayed if it rains.
why: Rain forces a replay. A replay for some other reason is still possible.

text: Team A qualifies only if it beats Team B.
nq: It does not beat Team B
why: Beating Team B is needed to qualify, but beating them alone may not be enough.

text: Asha plays unless she is injured.
why: "P unless Q" is "if not Q, then P": a fit Asha plays. The clue says nothing about an injured Asha, so playing hurt is not ruled out.

text: The flight leaves on time unless it is foggy.
why: No fog, then on time. Fog does not force a delay; it only lifts the promise.

text: Bilal does not travel unless Chitra travels too.
why: "Not P unless Q" is "P only if Q": Bilal travelling needs Chitra travelling. Chitra may go alone.

text: The fair is held outdoors unless it rains.
why: Dry weather means outdoors. In rain it may be outdoors or in; the clue does not say.

text: Dev is not picked unless Esha is picked.
why: "Not P unless Q": Dev is picked only if Esha is. Esha alone is fine.

text: The shop stays open unless the owner is ill.
why: A well owner means an open shop. An ill owner does not force it shut.

text: Unless Farhan comes, Gita will not come.
why: Without Farhan, no Gita: Gita comes only if Farhan does. Farhan may come alone.

text: Team X goes through unless it loses both games.
why: Win at least one game and Team X is through. Losing both does not by itself knock it out.

text: Hari takes the bus unless he is late.
np: He does not take the bus
why: On time, then the bus. Late, and he may still catch a bus.

text: Unless the trains run, the meeting is cancelled.
why: If the trains stop, the meeting is cancelled. With trains running it may still be cancelled for another reason.

text: Asha plays if and only if Bilal plays.
why: Each needs the other: they play together or not at all.

text: The lights are on exactly when the shop is open.
why: "Exactly when" runs both ways, like "if and only if".

text: Chitra is picked if Dev is, and only then.
why: "If Dev is" gives one direction, "and only then" the other.

text: Esha attends when, and only when, Farhan attends.
why: Both attend or neither does.

text: The bell rings if and only if the gate opens.
why: A ring means an open gate, and an open gate means a ring.

text: A team gets a bye if and only if it topped its group.
nq: It did not top its group
why: Group toppers get byes, and nobody else does.

text: Gita sits at an end if and only if Hari sits in the middle.
np: Gita is not at an end
nq: Hari is not in the middle
why: Either both happen or neither does.

text: The match goes to extra time if and only if the scores are level.
why: Level scores force extra time, and extra time means the scores were level.

text: Ravi wins the prize if, and only if, his team wins.
why: The commas do not change it: both directions hold.

text: Dev and Esha either both come or both stay away.
why: "Both or neither" is "if and only if" said another way.

text: Either Asha or Bilal is picked.
why: At least one is picked. Without "but not both", both may be.

text: Either Chitra or Dev is picked, but not both.
why: Exactly one: both and neither are ruled out.

text: Esha and Farhan are not both picked.
why: Only the pair together is ruled out. Neither being picked is fine.

text: Neither Gita nor Hari is picked.
why: Each of them is out, so only "neither" is left.

text: At least one of Ravi and Sana sings.
why: "At least one" allows both.

text: Exactly one of Team A and Team B qualifies.
why: Exactly one: not both, and not neither.

text: Asha cannot go if Bilal goes.
why: If Bilal goes, Asha does not: they never go together. Both staying is allowed.

text: Dev or Esha, but not both, sits at an end.
np: Dev is not at an end
nq: Esha is not at an end
why: One of them takes an end; the other does not.

text: Either the bus is late or the train is, or both.
why: "Or both" says it outright: only both on time is ruled out.

text: Farhan and Gita do not both sit next to Hari.
np: Farhan is not next to Hari
nq: Gita is not next to Hari
why: Hari can have one of them beside him, or neither, but not both.

text: Exactly two people sit between Asha and Dev.
why: Two people between means Dev is three seats from Asha.

text: At least two people sit between Asha and Dev.
why: Two or more between: seat 6 has two, seat 7 has three. On the left there is no room.

text: At most one person sits between Bilal and Chitra.
why: None or one between: right beside Bilal, or one seat further.

text: Exactly three people sit between Esha and Farhan, counting the shorter way round.
why: At a table of eight, three people between either way means Farhan sits opposite Esha.

text: Exactly one person sits between Ravi and Gita.
why: Gita is at the end, so the one seat with one person between is seat 3.

text: At least three people sit between Chitra and Dev.
why: Seat 6 leaves three between, seat 7 four.

text: At most two people sit between Farhan and Gita.
why: Anywhere from right beside Farhan to three seats away, on either side.

text: Exactly one person sits between Asha and Bilal, the shorter way round.
why: Two seats round from Asha, in either direction.

text: Exactly two people sit between Esha and Dev, and Esha sits to Dev's left.
why: Three seats to Dev's left: seat 2.

text: Exactly one person sits between Chitra and Bilal.
why: Two seats from Bilal on either side: seats 2 and 6.

text: Bilal sits immediately to the left of Asha.
why: The very next seat on Asha's left: seat 2.

text: Bilal sits to the left of Asha.
why: No "immediately", so any seat on Asha's left fits.

text: Dev sits somewhere to the right of Chitra.
why: Any seat to Chitra's right: 6 or 7.

text: Farhan sits immediately to the right of Esha.
why: Only the next seat on Esha's right.

text: The person from Pune sits somewhere to the left of the person from Chennai.
why: Clue 10 of the six colleagues: any seat left of seat 5.

text: The doctor sits immediately to the left of Asha.
why: Seat 2, right beside Asha on her left.

text: Esha sits somewhere to the right of Dev.
why: Any of the four seats to Dev's right.

text: Gita sits immediately to the left of Farhan.
why: Seat 2 only.

text: Ishaan sits to the right of Hari.
why: Seats 6, 7 and 8 all lie to Hari's right.

text: The person from Pune sits immediately to the left of the person from Delhi.
why: Clue 11 of the six colleagues: the seat just left of Delhi.

text: Dev sits between Asha and Bilal.
why: Anywhere on the stretch from Asha to Bilal: seats 2, 3 and 4.

text: Chitra sits in a seat between seats 2 and 6.
why: Seats 3, 4 and 5. The named seats are the edges.

text: Gita sits between Esha and Farhan.
why: Seats 3, 4 and 5 lie between them.

text: Hari sits between seats 3 and 7.
why: Seats 4, 5 and 6.

text: Dev sits between Bilal and Asha.
why: The order the names come in does not matter: seats 3, 4 and 5.

text: Sana sits between seats 1 and 5, but not next to Ravi.
why: Between seats 1 and 5 is 2, 3 and 4; seat 4 is next to Ravi.

text: Esha sits between seats 1 and 4.
why: Seats 2 and 3.

text: Bilal sits between Asha and Chitra.
why: Seats 2 and 3, the two between them.

text: Ishaan sits between Gita and Hari.
why: Seats 4, 5 and 6.

text: Jaya sits between seats 4 and 8.
why: Seats 5, 6 and 7.

text: Bilal sits immediately to the left of Asha.
why: Facing the centre from the bottom seat, Asha's left is your left: seat 2.

text: Bilal sits immediately to the left of Asha.
why: Facing away from the centre, Asha's left is the other way round: seat 6.

text: Dev sits immediately to the left of Chitra.
why: They face you, so their left is your right: seat 4.

text: Farhan sits second to the right of Esha.
why: Two seats to Esha's right, one person between: seat 7.

text: Hari sits third to the left of Gita.
why: Three seats round to Gita's left: seat 4.

text: Bilal sits second to the right of Asha.
why: Facing out, Asha's right runs the way the seat numbers do: seat 3.

text: Sana sits somewhere to the right of Ravi.
why: Facing you, Ravi's right is your left: seats 1, 2 and 3.

text: Chitra sits immediately to the right of Bilal.
why: Bilal sits at the top, facing down towards the centre, so his right is your left: seat 3.

text: Dev sits second to the left of Esha.
why: Two seats to Esha's left, with one person between: seat 2.

text: The Branding specialist sits second to the left of Ishaan.
why: Clue 7 of the seven consultants: two seats round to Ishaan's left, seat 3.
